blocks.text: Personal and Confidential
Re: Freedom-to-operate analysis
Dear Ms. Blair:

Thank you for asking us to act for {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} on the question of whether it is free to bring its new product to market. This letter records the work we have agreed to do, who will do it, what it will cost, and the terms on which we will act, and once you have countersigned it, it is the agreement between us.
Please read it with care, and tell me before you sign if any part of it differs from your understanding of what we discussed, so that we can correct the letter before the work begins.
What We Will Do

We will analyze whether the product that {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} intends to launch, in the configuration your team documents for us at the outset, can be made, used, offered for sale, or sold in the United States, or imported into it, without infringing any claim of an unexpired United States patent. We will also review published United States applications whose claims, if they issued in their present form or in a form reasonably supported by the specification, could reach that configuration.

Where a claim appears to read on the product, we will set out the available non-infringement positions, the prospects for a design change that avoids the claim, and, at the level needed to judge the risk, any substantial question about the claim's validity. Our conclusions will be stated in a written memorandum addressed to you and marked as privileged.
What Falls Outside This Engagement

The engagement does not include a formal opinion on the validity or enforceability of any patent, a search of patents or applications outside the United States, the preparation of patent applications for {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}}, or representation in any licensing negotiation, dispute, or proceeding before a court or the Patent Trial and Appeal Board. Any of those would require a separate letter.
How the Work Will Proceed
The work will move through four stages, each of which depends on the one before it:

items: 1. Definition. Your team provides the drawings, specifications, and bill of materials for the launch configuration, and we confirm in writing the revision we will analyze.
2. Search. We search issued patents and published applications by classification, keyword, and citation, and we keep a dated log of every search so that the result can be checked and repeated.
3. Review. We read each reference that survives an initial screen against the confirmed revision, and we prepare claim charts, together with the file history, for any claim that warrants close study.
4. Opinion. We deliver the memorandum described above, with the search log, the list of references reviewed, and the claim charts on which it relies.

blocks.text: The search speaks as of the date on which we close it, so applications that publish after that date, and patents that issue from them, fall outside the opinion unless you ask us to update it. A change to the product after we confirm the revision is likewise outside the opinion until we have analyzed it, and we will tell you in writing what that further analysis would involve before we begin it.
Who Will Do the Work

Heather Munoz, a partner of the firm, will lead the engagement and will sign the opinion. Richard Henderson and Kelly Snyder, both registered patent agents, will carry out the search and the technical review of the references under her supervision, and because conclusions on infringement are legal conclusions, those conclusions will be reached and stated by Ms. Munoz.
I will remain responsible for the relationship and for the terms of this letter, and you should raise with me directly any concern you have about staffing, cost, or the pace of the work.
Fee and Commencement

Our fee for the engagement as scoped above is a fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2020-001.fee}}. Work will begin on {{fact:f:E-2020-001.start}}, and we expect it to run about nine months from that date, although the length of the review stage depends on how many references the search returns and cannot be fixed in advance.

The fixed fee covers the four stages described above and nothing else. Work outside that scope, including any update of the search after the opinion issues, will be billed at our standard hourly rates, and only after you have approved it in writing.
Fees and Payment

We will invoice the fixed fee in three equal installments: the first at commencement, the second when we close the search, and the third on delivery of the opinion. Invoices are due within thirty days of their date, and costs such as commercial database charges and copies of file histories are billed at cost in addition to the fee.

If an invoice remains unpaid sixty days after its date, we may suspend work until it is paid, after giving you written notice that we intend to do so. We are not responsible for any delay that results from a suspension, and if the invoice remains unpaid after that notice we may withdraw on the terms set out under Term and Termination.
Conflicts

We have checked {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} and the parties you identified to us against our records and found no conflict that prevents us from acting. A search of this kind can, however, return a patent owned by a current client of this firm, and if it does we will tell you promptly and may need to refer the analysis of that patent to independent counsel.
Term and Termination

This engagement begins on the date stated above and ends when we deliver the opinion, unless it ends earlier under this paragraph. You may end it at any time by written notice, and we may end it by written notice for nonpayment, for a conflict that cannot be resolved, or where the rules of professional conduct require or permit us to withdraw.

If the engagement ends before the opinion issues, you will owe the installments already invoiced, a pro rata share of the next installment for work performed to the date of the notice, and costs incurred to that date. We will return your materials on request.
Confidentiality and Privilege

We will hold in confidence the information and documents you give us in the course of the engagement and will use them only for this work. Our communications with you, and the opinion itself, are intended to be protected by the attorney-client privilege, and that protection can be lost if they are shared beyond the people at {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} who need them in order to make decisions.
We therefore ask that you keep distribution of the opinion to that group, and that you speak to us before sharing any part of our analysis with customers, investors, suppliers, or insurers.
Limitation of Liability

An opinion of this kind is a professional judgment on the documents available at the date of the search; it is not a guarantee that no patent owner will assert a claim against {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}}, or that a court would read a claim as we do. Our conclusions depend on the accuracy and completeness of the product information you give us, and we are not responsible for an error that results from information that was inaccurate or incomplete when we received it.

To the extent the rules governing lawyers permit, our liability arising out of this engagement is limited to the fees paid under it, and nothing in this letter limits any liability that those rules do not allow us to limit.
Governing Law

This letter is governed by the law of the state in which the firm maintains its office, without regard to that state's conflict-of-laws rules. If any provision is held unenforceable, the remaining provisions continue in effect.

If these terms are acceptable, please sign in the space provided below and return a copy to me. When I have it, Richard Henderson will send you the list of drawings and specifications we need in order to confirm the launch configuration, and the work will start from that list.
Very truly yours,

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL
ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
What the opinion has to answer

We owe {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} one opinion, signed by Heather Munoz. It says whether the client's launch product can be sold in the United States without infringing a live claim. Everything below exists to put the evidence for that opinion in front of her in a form she can check.

The engagement began on {{fact:f:E-2020-001.start}}. The fee is fixed, so time spent outside the scope of the engagement letter comes out of the firm. If a request looks like new work, raise it with Heather before doing it.
Our contact at the client is Barbara Blair, Director of Operations. Document requests go through her and nobody else. That way we keep one record of what we asked for and what arrived.
We do not yet have the product documents. Until we do, any assumption about the design is provisional. Write it down in the matter file so Heather can see it and strike it if it is wrong.
The work, in order

items: 1. Product definition. Barbara Blair sends drawings, specification, bill of materials, and a feature list for the launch configuration. We freeze one revision and analyze that revision only. A later revision is a scope change and goes to Heather before anyone works on it.

2. Search. Kelly Snyder runs the first pass: classification, keyword, and forward and backward citation from any reference the client already knows of. Every query goes in the search log with its date and database.
3. Screen. I read the first pass against the feature list and put each reference in one of three groups: remote, second read, chart. Kelly takes the second reads.
4. Claim charts. I chart each independent claim in the chart group, element by element, against the frozen revision. Dependent claims get charted only where the independent claim is close.
5. File histories. For every charted patent we order the file history and note each amendment and argument that narrowed the claim. Most of our non-infringement positions will come from there.

6. Design-around notes. Where a claim reads, or nearly reads, I record what the product would have to change to avoid it. The client's engineers judge what the change costs. We judge whether it avoids the claim.
7. Opinion. Heather drafts and signs. Kelly and I assemble the appendix: search log, reference list, claim charts, and file history notes.

blocks.text: Items 2 through 6 will overlap once the search is running. Item 1 will not. Nothing gets charted against a revision we have not frozen.

Kelly has asked that we track hours against each item from the first day, given the fixed fee. I agree. Log time to the item number, not only to the matter, so that Heather can see which items are using the budget.
Before the end of next week
The search cannot start properly until the configuration is fixed. So the document request goes out first, and the rest waits on it.

items: I will send Barbara Blair the document request early next week, with a short note on what we mean by launch configuration.
Kelly: set up the search log and the reference tracker in the matter folder, and draft the first classification list as soon as the feature list arrives.
Heather: confirm how we treat applications that publish after the search closes, and whether you want the cutoff stated on the face of the opinion.
Docketing: calendar a monthly check of newly published applications in our classes for the life of the engagement, starting when the search closes.

blocks.text: If anything here conflicts with the engagement letter, the letter controls. Tell me and I will correct this memo.
Hello Barbara,

The first search pass is finished, and we are now screening what it returned. I am starting this thread so that our status updates on the freedom-to-operate work for {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} sit in one place. Heather and Kelly are copied and will add to it as the work moves.

Where things stand. We are analyzing the revision your team sent us last month. The search covered issued United States patents and published applications, and every query is logged so the search can be checked and repeated. The screen is about a third done. Some references will need closer study, and I will give you a count once the screen is complete.
Before the screen goes further, three things from your side would help:

items: Confirm that the revision we have is the one going to launch. If anything has changed, tell me before we chart against it.
Send us any patent numbers or owner names your engineers already know of in this area. A bare list is enough.
Give us an hour with one of your engineers in the next two weeks. Two features are not settled by the drawings, and we need an engineer's answer on both.

blocks.text: Thanks
Dear Barbara,

One point on the second item in Richard's note, the list of patents your engineers already know of. Please have it sent to Richard or to me, and ask the engineers at {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} not to discuss those patents with each other by email.

An engineer's views on a third-party patent are not privileged unless they are given to counsel. Written comments of that kind can be produced in litigation and read as knowledge of the patent. A bare list of numbers or owner names carries none of that risk.
If an engineer has a concern about a particular patent, the place for it is the call Richard has asked for, with one of us on the line.
Best
Hello Barbara,
On the engineering call, Heather will take the part on any patent your engineers raise. I will run the rest of the hour.
So that the time is well used, this is what I plan to cover, in order:

items: the two features the drawings leave open;
which components you buy in rather than make, and from which suppliers;
whether any supplier agreement gives {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} an indemnity for patent claims.

blocks.text: The last two matter because a bought-in part can still put the product at risk, and an indemnity changes who carries that risk. Any afternoon next week suits us. If you send me two or three times, I will set it up.
Thanks
Dear Barbara,
I will be on the call for the full hour, not only the patent questions. The supplier point Richard raised is one I want to hear first hand.

If any supplier agreement does carry an indemnity, please send us the clause itself and not a summary of it. The wording decides whether it covers a claim against the finished product or only against the part, and those are very different protections.
None of this changes the schedule for {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}}. Richard will confirm the time once you have sent him your options.
Best
